name: Victorian Corsetry
summary: The factory-made corset of the Victorian age. It has coutil cloth, a steel busk, metal eyelets and spring-steel bones, shaped with gussets into an hourglass. It was worn under the crinoline and the bustle.

philosophy.core_thesis: The dress is only as good as the foundation: a firm, shaped corset gives the hourglass that the outer cloth then covers.
design_principles: Cut the corset in 8 to 12 panels, and add a gusset at the bust and at the hip to give the curve.
Close the front with a steel busk of two flat plates, and lace the back through metal eyelets.
Set a bone or a steel strip in each seam, and one at each side of the busk and of the eyelets.
Make the body of coutil, a tight cotton herringbone twill that does not stretch.
Reduce the waist 5 to 10 cm below the natural waist; use a long busk of 30 to 35 cm.
Add a satin or a broché cover for show, with a narrow lace edge at the top.
Keep a plain cotton chemise under the corset and a corset cover over it.
anti_patterns: A soft bodice with no bone or busk
The flat, conical front of the eighteenth century
Stretch cloth that moves with the body
A bare, unlined cotton with no coutil
A short brassiere with no waist control

silhouette.shape: An hourglass: a high bust, a small waist and a full hip, with a long, hard front.
silhouette.line: A smooth curve from the bust to the hip; the busk keeps the front flat and the back is laced close.
silhouette.fit: Close and firm on the waist and the ribs; the gussets give room at the bust and the hip.
silhouette.proportion: Waist 50 to 58 cm for fashion; length 30 to 40 cm at the front; the busk 30 to 35 cm long.
rules: Make the waist 15 to 20 cm smaller than the bust and the hip.
Run a flat steel busk from the bust to the stomach.
Add a gusset at the bust and at the hip so that the cloth lies smooth.
Cut the top edge low, so that the corset does not show under a day bodice.
Lengthen the corset below the waist in the 1870s, so that it holds the hip down to the thigh.

fabrics.rule: Build the body in coutil, shape it with whalebone and spring steel, and cover it with satin, with a lace edge.

methods: panels cut to a paper pattern in sizes
gussets at the bust and the hip
bone or steel in each seam
metal eyelets set by a machine
sewing machine seams in a factory
construction.closures: A busk of two steel plates at the front, with studs and loops; the back laces through metal eyelets, with a cord.
construction.details: Gussets, a lace edge at the top, silk embroidery along the bones, suspender tabs for the stockings, and a small bow at the front.

surface.pattern: Plain white or drab coutil for day; for evening, satin with a flower stitch along each bone, called flossing.
surface.gloss: Coutil at 3–8 GU; satin at 30–60 GU.
surface.wear: A worn corset has a bent bone, a creased waist and a grey stain on the coutil. The eyelets rust if they are of low grade.

palette.strategy: White, drab and black for the daily corset; a deep colour or pale silk for the corset that shows.

processes: layered panels sewn on a machine
channels cut and filled with bone or steel
eyelets punched and set by a machine
making.scale: Made in a factory in standard sizes from the 1850s, with some made to measure.
making.signs: A steel busk, metal eyelets, a gusset at the bust and the hip, a bone in each seam, and a maker's stamp on the inside.

pieces.form: Long-busk corset with gussets, in white coutil
Evening corset in satin with silk flossing along the bones
Cage of spring-steel hoops on cotton tapes
Starched cotton petticoat with a flounce
Chemise of fine cotton under the corset

canonical_works.work: Health corset shown at the Great Exhibition
Pink silk and whalebone corset worn at a wedding

evidence.title: Doll's cotton corset with a lace-up front, about 1890s

emotion.target_response: A sense of propriety and control: a firm waist, a straight back and a body shaped for the dress above it.

use_cases: a museum label or object study
avoid_when: the brief wants the eighteenth-century conical stays
the brief wants a soft or stretch bra

modifiers.how: Lengthen the busk, flatten the stomach, push the hip back, and keep the steel and coutil.
Remove the gussets and the steel busk, cut a cone, and bone it with whalebone in linen.
Add the cage crinoline or the bustle and a layered silk skirt over the corset.

ornament_level.note: The day corset is plain; the evening corset carries lace and flossing.
